questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements: 1. Ocean currents are the slow-surface movement of water in the ocean. 2. Ocean currents assist in maintaining the Earth's heat balance 3. Ocean currents are set in motion primarily by prevailing winds 4. Ocean currents are affected by the configuration of the ocean. Which of these statements are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2002] Consider the following statements: 1. Ocean currents are the slow-surface movement of water in the ocean. 2. Ocean currents assist in maintaining the Earth's heat balance 3. Ocean currents are set in motion primarily by prevailing winds 4. Ocean currents are affected by the configuration of the ocean. Which of these statements are correct?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D) 1, 2, 3 and 4. The flow of ocean water in a particular direction is called the oceanic current. Mostly ocean currents are set in motion by the prevailing wind. If the wind is blow, normally the surface water is in motion. [I.A.S. (Pre) 2002]

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following factors is responsible for the change in the regular direction of the ocean currents in the Indian Ocean?
questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997] Which one of the following factors is responsible for the change in the regular direction of the ocean currents in the Indian Ocean?
optionsEn: Indian Ocean is half an Ocean
Indian Ocean is a land-locked ocean
Indian Ocean has greater variation in salinity
optionsHi: Indian Ocean is half an Ocean
Indian Ocean is a land-locked ocean
Indian Ocean has greater variation in salinity
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B) Indian Ocean has Monsoon drift. The ocean currents of the Indian Ocean are slightly different from the Pacific and the Atlantic Ocean. Land and monsoon winds have a major impact on the Indian Oceanic current. The direction of current flow changes twice in the Northern Indian Ocean due to the North-East and South-West monsoon winds whereas Southern Indian Ocean currents have a defi nite pattern. [I.A.S. (Pre) 1997]

questions.questionTextEn: The country benefiting the most out of the North Atlantic Drift is :
questions.questionTextHi: [R.A.S./R.T.S.(Pre) 1999] The country benefiting the most out of the North Atlantic Drift is :
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C) Norway. Northern Atlantic currents generate near 45 o north latitude and 45o west meridian. It takes away the water of warm Gulf stream towards, Europe, where Norway, situated in the sub- polar region, is benefited most by this current. This benefit is in such a way that when at the onset of winter chances of most of the countries of Europe coming under the expansion of ice-covering becomes greater than warm north Atlantic currents block the expansion of ice-cover and therefore this current is also known as 'Blanket of Europe'. [R.A.S./R.T.S.(Pre) 1999]

questions.questionTextHi: [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023] Which of the following statements is true?
optionsEn: Ocean salinity is maximum at the Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.
Tide comes on the earth every day after exactly 12 hours 30 minutes.
Benguela current is a cold current of the Pacific ocean.
If the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are in a straight line then this situation is the situation of small tide.
optionsHi: Ocean salinity is maximum at the Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.
Tide comes on the earth every day after exactly 12 hours 30 minutes.
Benguela current is a cold current of the Pacific ocean.
If the Sun, the Earth and the Moon are in a straight line then this situation is the situation of small tide.
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A) Ocean salinity is maximum at the Tropic of Cancer and Capricorn.. Ocean salinity is the term used to defi ne the total content of dissolved salts in sea water.It is usually expressed as parts per thousand (‰) or ppt.Ocean salinity is maximum at the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic by Capricorn due to low rainfall and high evaporation. Hence statement (a) is correct. The periodical rise and fall of the sea level, once or twice a day, mainly due to the attraction of the Sun and the Moon, is called a tide. [U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023]

questions.questionTextEn: What explains the eastward flow of the equatorial counter-current?
questions.questionTextHi: [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015] What explains the eastward flow of the equatorial counter-current?
optionsEn: The Earth's rotation on its axis
Convergence of the two equatorial currents
Occurrence of the Belt of Calm near the equator
optionsHi: The Earth's rotation on its axis
Convergence of the two equatorial currents
Occurrence of the Belt of Calm near the equator
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B) Convergence of the two equatorial currents. There are two equatorial currents flowing from east to west – the north equatorial current and the south equatorial current. In between these two, there fl ows an equatorial counter current in the opposite direction from west to east. Piling up of water due to the convergence of two equatorial currents give rise to equatorial counter current. [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015]
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) Convergence of the two equatorial currents। व्याख्या (22. The Ocean Currents — The Ocean Currents): There are two equatorial currents flowing from east to west – the north equatorial current and the south equatorial current. In between these two, there fl ows an equatorial counter current in the opposite direction from west to east. Piling up of water due to the convergence of two equatorial currents give rise to equatorial counter current. [I.A.S. (Pre) 2015]

Warm Ocean currents— Brazil current, Gulf stream, Kuroshio current, etc. Cold currents - Falkland current, Labrador current, Canary current. [U.P. R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2017]
